newsitem.title: USA: Will seek prompt change in Japan liquor taxes-U.S..
newsitem.headline: Will seek prompt change in Japan liquor taxes-U.S..

text.p: The United States will seek "prompt implementation" of a World Trade Organization ruling that Japan should eliminate discriminatory taxes on imported liquor, Acting Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky said Friday.
The ruling by the WTO appellate body could remove a major barrier to sales of U.S. whiskey, vodka and other distilled spirits to Japan, her office said.
Japan is the No 2 export market for U.S. liquor, despite heavy taxes on whiskey and Western-type distilled spirits, and is a $100 million a year market.

Canada, the European Union and the United States filed a complaint before WTO in July 1995 against the taxes, which they said were many times higher than those on shochu, a traditional Japanese spirit.
WTO ruled against Japan two months ago but it appealed.
Barshefsky's office said the appellate ruling buttressed a 1987 ruling that the liquor taxes were discriminatory.
"Given the long-standing nature of this dispute, we will work to ensure prompt implementation by Japan," she said.
The appellate ruling found the tax system discriminatory and recommended Japan eliminate the bias, her office said.
